data.title: Binance says 90% of stolen crypto assets replenished after $6.3 billion security breach
data.description:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Saturday that it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover losses from a $6.3 billion security breach, with around 90% of the stolen token assets already replenished. The exchange said it is working to restore withdrawal services in phases.

In its second security incident recovery update, Binance said it would absorb the entire financial impact of the theft through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate treasury, ensuring that users do not bear the losses.

"Our last update explained that Binance had set aside more than $6.34B in company funds to cover hacked losses, and we had already covered approximately 80% of the impacted amount of the hacked loss at that time," the exchange said in a statement.

"That covered amount is now up to 90%," it added.

Binance said Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH), Tether (USDT), BNB, Solana (SOL), USD Coin (USDC), XRP, USD1, RLUSD and ZEC were fully backed. It would continue buying the remaining relevant token assets through market and over-the-counter (OTC) channels until coverage reached 100% for all tokens.

The exchange said it had already secured $5 billion in the same digital assets that were stolen, including USDC, USDT, Bitcoin, Ether and BNB. In its earlier update, this represented approximately 80% of the impacted amount.

Binance confirmed that its hot wallets were compromised at around 20:05 UTC on October 29, resulting in unauthorised withdrawals of approximately $6.3 billion worth of digital assets.

As part of its recovery efforts, the exchange said around $3 billion in stolen assets had been frozen on blockchain networks through coordination with law enforcement agencies, blockchain intelligence firms, asset issuers and industry partners.

The company said its technical team was targeting the phased resumption of withdrawals within approximately 34 hours, subject to the completion of security checks. Deposits and other unaffected platform services remained operational.

Binance also announced plans to publish an updated Proof of Reserves report by Monday, November 2, allowing users to verify the digital assets backing their account balances.

On the cause of the breach, the exchange said its initial investigation had pointed to a compromised laptop, but subsequent findings had revealed additional points of intrusion.

"Our initial investigation suggested that the incident may involve a compromised laptop, however, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," it said.

The company reiterated that it had found no evidence of wallet private keys being leaked. Further technical findings were expected within approximately 48 hours, subject to verification.

Meanwhile, blockchain investigation firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis have linked the $6.3 billion theft to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor, according to Reuters.

Cybersecurity experts cited by Reuters said proceeds from North Korean cryptocurrency thefts have helped fund the country's weapons programmes.

Binance has not publicly confirmed who was responsible for the attack and said its investigation remains ongoing.

The exchange said it would publish a detailed technical report outlining how the breach occurred and the additional security measures being introduced to prevent similar incidents.

data.title: He Lost His Job Over a Year Ago. Now He Asks for Help With His Financial Plan — WSJ
data.description:
By Lisa Ward

Kevin McCann is actively looking for a new job. In the meantime, he wants to make sure he is managing his savings wisely.

The 44-year-old from Chicago lost his position as a senior product manager at a tech startup over a year ago, where he earned upward of $200,000 a year including bonuses. He currently earns $20,000 from freelancing. His unemployment benefits ran out last November.

McCann, who is unmarried, has two 401(k)s from his previous employers totaling about $260,000 and a traditional IRA with about $160,000; the accounts are invested in about 80% equities and 20% fixed income. He is considering converting one or both of the accounts to a Roth IRA to take advantage of his current low income, which would mitigate the taxes he would owe on the conversion.

He already has a Roth with about $81,000, about $10,000 of which is in cash that could be used in an emergency. With the Roth, McCann can withdraw his original after-tax contribution without an early-withdrawal penalty or any additional taxes.

He also has almost $270,000 in a brokerage account. About $94,000 is invested in U.S. Treasury bonds that mature in one to six months, which he currently is tapping to supplement his income.

He has about $7,000 in a checking account, $6,000 in a health savings account and about $13,000 in six-month Series I savings bonds.

McCann owns a condo currently valued at about $625,000, with a $344,000 mortgage and a 2.99% interest rate. He pays $2,600 monthly, including taxes and HOA fees, and the mortgage is his only debt outstanding.

Other monthly expenses include $1,400 for groceries, eating out and entertainment, $150 for gas and public transportation, $200 for general shopping and $250 every six months for car insurance.

McCann currently has no health insurance. He looked at buying a high-deductible plan, but the plans cost about $400 a month, which he thought was too high given his current circumstances.

He says he has reduced his spending from $7,000 to $5,000 monthly since the job loss.

Advice from a pro

Jarrett Solomon, a certified financial planner and partner at Connecticut Wealth Management in Farmington, Conn., suggests McCann first rethink his decision to forgo health insurance. Paying $400 monthly for a high-deductible plan or looking for catastrophic coverage is worthwhile, he says, because an unexpected serious illness or injury could drastically alter McCann's financial well-being if he lacks coverage.

Solomon doesn't recommend converting either the 401(k) or traditional IRA into a Roth, because the taxes he would owe on the money he withdraws for the conversion might be too costly for McCann right now, even though he's currently in a lower tax bracket than he will be when he finds full-time employment.

Similarly, Solomon suggests McCann hold off on contributing to the HSA even if he decides to buy a high-deductible health plan. The money can only be used for qualifying healthcare expenses (otherwise income tax is owed on the amount withdrawn, and there's a steep penalty if you are under age 65), and he needs to be able to easily access his savings right now.

One move McCann can make to take advantage of temporarily being in a lower income-tax bracket is to sell some of his most profitable mutual funds in his taxable brokerage account and buy them back.

That could help reduce capital-gains taxes he might owe in the future, when his income is higher, because any gains at that point would be calculated from the price he pays for the funds now, rather than the lower price he paid earlier. And he wouldn't have to pay federal capital-gains taxes on the sale now as long as his taxable income is lower than $50,000, though he might still have to pay state tax.

He also might choose to keep some of the proceeds from the sale more liquid in case finding a new job takes longer than expected.

Solomon says McCann should look for ways to reduce monthly expenses, particularly on food and utilities.

Finally, Solomon suggests McCann can maximize long-term growth in his retirement accounts by investing more aggressively — changing the asset allocation to 90% or even 100% equities. He can use the brokerage account for more-conservative fixed-income investments as well as cash.

data.title: Earnings scorecard: 21 out of 22 technology companies beat EPS estimates this week
data.description:
Information technology stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major companies, including Microsoft , Intel , and Sandisk .

In this week's earnings recap, 22 tickers reported results, out of which 21 companies reported earnings beats and 20 beat revenue expectations.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Microsoft shares rose in extended trading on Wednesday after the Windows maker reported fiscal first-quarter results that topped/missed estimates.

For the period ending Sept. 30, Microsoft said it earned an adjusted $4.89 per share as revenue rose 19% year-over-year (17% in constant currency) to come in at $92.28B. Cloud revenue came in at $63.9B, above the $61.62B estimate. Azure revenue rose 48%, above the estimate of 44.8%.

On the company's earnings call, Microsoft management said it expects fiscal second-quarter revenue to be between $96B and $97.1B, above the $95.63B estimate.

On the other hand, Intel shares plunged 26% in premarket trading on Friday after it issued fourth quarter guidance that missed Wall Street's estimates by a considerable margin.

The semiconductor giant expects its Q4 revenue to be between $15B and $16B, below estimates of $17.05B. Adjusted earnings are forecast to be $0.25 per share, below the $0.43 estimate. Adjusted gross margins are expected to be 38%, below the 42.8% estimate.

Sandisk shares erased initial losses and rose 3% in extended trading on Thursday as the storage maker reported fiscal first-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast by a considerable margin.

Shares have gained more than 380% year-to-date.

For the period ending Oct. 2, Sandisk said it earned an adjusted $49.51 per share as revenue rose 23% year-over-year to come in at $11.03B. Analysts had expected Sandisk to earn an adjusted $46.67 per share on $10.72B in revenue.

Looking ahead to the fiscal second-quarter, Sandisk said it expects to earn between $55 and $57 per share on an adjusted basis, above the $52.60 per share estimate. Sales are forecast to be between $12.2B and $12.6B, with the $12.4B midpoint above the $12.31B estimate.

For the upcoming week, Apple , Qualcomm , Advanced Micro Devices , Palantir Technologies , and Super Micro Computer are among the key information technology companies that are scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Muthoot Finance posts 27% rise in PAT at ₹2,977 crore  in Q2 FY27
data.description:
Gold loan lender Muthoot Finance Ltd has registered a 27 per cent increase in its profit after tax (PAT) at ₹2,977 crore as against ₹2,345 crores in Q2 FY26.

The company registered a PAT of ₹5,527 crore in H1 FY27 as against ₹4,391 crore in H1 FY26, an increase of 26 per cent y-o-y. Loan AUM stood at ₹1,87,810 crore in H1 FY27 as compared to ₹1,32,305 crore in H1 FY26, registering a growth of 42 per cent y-o-y. During Q2 FY27, gold loan AUM increased by ₹15,658 crore.

Consolidated PAT for H1 FY27 increased to ₹6,103 crore as against ₹4,386 crore last year, an increase of 39 per cent y-o-y. Consolidated Loan AUM grew by 42 per cent y-o-y to ₹2,09,317 crore in H1 FY27 as against ₹1,47,673 crore in H1 FY26. During the half year, consolidated Loan Assets Under Management grew by ₹27,401 crore, growth of 15 per cent.

Alexander George Muthoot, Managing Director, said, “We are revising our gold loan growth guidance for FY27 upward by an additional 10 per cent. The RBI’s updated gold lending guidelines, effective April 1, 2026, involves a learning curve for us as well as customers, which will get stabilised over few quarters irrespective of which growth trajectory will continue.”

“During the quarter Muthoot Finance added 201 branches further expanding the reach across the length and breadth of the country. India’s gold loan market continues to evolve, with new entrants and rising demand creating opportunities for responsible growth. Our focus remains on strengthening our services through customer trust, deeper reach and technology-led service delivery, while maintaining prudent lending practices and sustaining our growth momentum through FY27,” he added.

data.title: Rainbow Children’s Medicare Q2: Revenue rises 23%, profit grows 11%
data.description:
Rainbow Children’s Medicare reported a 23% year-on-year increase in revenue for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The firm reported revenue of 548 crore, up from 444 crore same quarter last year.

EBITDA grew 14%, while profit after tax (PAT) rose 11% during the quarter. PAT came at 83.9 crore compare to 75.6 crore last year.

The company said inpatient and outpatient volumes remained healthy despite seasonal softness due to a significant shortfall in monsoon rainfall. It attributed the growth to patient volumes, improving performance across hospitals and initiatives focused on digital engagement and community outreach.

Rainbow said these initiatives are translating into higher outpatient department (OPD) footfalls and inpatient admissions.

Expansion in Andhra Pradesh

The company has commenced operations at a newly acquired 70-bed hospital in Nellore and a new 50-bed hospital in Guntur, strengthening its presence in Coastal Andhra Pradesh. These additions extend its network from Visakhapatnam to Chennai.

Rainbow also plans to establish a specialised paediatric hospital in Amaravati in phases, with an initial capacity of 150 beds. The project follows the allotment of two acres of land by the Andhra Pradesh government and is currently in the planning phase.

The company said its recently launched hospitals in Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh, and HRBR, Mahadevapura and Electronic City in Bengaluru are progressing as expected and have been integrated into its operating model.

Updates on upcoming projects

Rainbow expects to commence operations at its Indore hospital in Q3 FY27. At its Malad facility in Mumbai, project work has been completed and interior work is underway, with operations targeted for Q1 FY28.

Construction of its approximately 130-bed regional hub hospital in Coimbatore is progressing, with operations expected to begin in Q3 FY28. The company is also developing two facilities in Gurugram — a 125-bed spoke hospital in Sector 56, targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY28, and a 325-bed hub hospital in Sector 44, expected to begin operations in Q1 FY29.

Development work is continuing on a 150-bed regional hub hospital in Pune and an 80-bed spoke hospital in Seegehalli, both of which are expected to commence operations in FY29.

Commenting on the performance, Chairman and Managing Director Ramesh Kancharla said the expansion in Nellore and Guntur strengthens the company's presence across Andhra Pradesh, while the proposed Amaravati hospital has moved into the project planning phase.

CEO Abarali Dalal said the company had recorded year-on-year revenue growth of more than 20% for the third consecutive quarter. He attributed the performance to the onboarding of doctors, healthy occupancy and operational efficiencies, adding that new hospitals were steadily ramping up and contributing to network growth.

Rainbow said its focus remains on improving occupancy, maintaining patient throughput and sustaining growth across mature and new hospitals.

Rainbow Children’s Medicare shares ended 2.27% higher at ₹1,224 on October 30, gaining ₹27.20.

data.title: Marketing industry leaders and experts explore AI impact at VIT Chennai Marketing Conclave
data.description:
The VIT Business School, VIT Chennai on Friday organised a Marketing Conclave bringing together industry leaders, marketing professionals and entrepreneurs to explore consumer behaviour, brand building and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence (AI).

The event saw Lakshminarayanan Duraiswamy, Managing Director, Sundaram Home Finance Limited, deliver the keynote address, and LV Navneeth, Chief Executive Officer, THG Publishing Private Ltd (The Hindu), also delivered a special keynote address.

Emphasising the importance of customer trust in an increasingly AI-driven business environment, Duraiswamy said that organisations must earn customers’ trust and continue to strengthen it every day. Technology and innovation should always be guided by customer needs, he said.

“AI is not about creating a new technology, and it is not about creating a new design. It is about what it does for the customer,” he added.

Imagining the Future

Speaking on the theme “Imagining the Future", Navneeth urged young people to cultivate the ability to reflect, imagine and execute ideas. The constant pressure to remain busy often leaves little time for meaningful reflection, which is essential for innovation and creative thinking, he observed.

Thyagarajan T, Pro-Vice Chancellor, VIT Chennai; Suresh Balakrishna, Consultant, VIT Chennai; and Saju B, Dean, VIT Business School, VIT Chennai, also addressed the gathering.

The conclave featured three panel discussions and two fireside chats, providing a platform for industry experts to exchange perspectives on emerging marketing trends, changing consumer expectations and the impact of technology on brand strategy.

The first panel discussion, titled “The Human Edge: Understanding Consumers in the Age of AI", examined the continuing importance of human understanding and consumer insights in technology-driven marketing. The second panel explored strategies for building meaningful consumer relationships and lasting brand loyalty.

Another panel focused on the changing branding landscape, examining the challenges and opportunities emerging from the growth of direct-to-consumer (D2C) business models.

The Marketing Conclave also provided a forum for students and industry professionals to exchange ideas on the future of marketing.

data.title: Birla Corporation Q2 profit plunges 58.9% to ₹37 crore on higher input costs
data.description:
Birla Corporation Ltd on Saturday reported a 58.9 per cent year-on-year moderation in consolidated net profit to Rs 37 crore for the September quarter, as higher input costs and weak cement prices hit margins.

The company had posted a net profit of Rs 90 crore in the same period a year ago.

Revenue rises, but EBITDA declines

Consolidated revenue rose 9 per cent to Rs 2,441 crore from Rs 2,233 crore a year earlier. Consolidated EBITDA declined to Rs 254 crore from Rs 332 crore.

Cement sales volume grew 7 per cent to 4.54 million tonnes, while realisation rose 2 per cent to Rs 4,925 per tonne, though it was marginally lower sequentially as prices weakened in core markets through July and August. Capacity utilisation was steady at 85 per cent.

Higher input costs squeeze cement margins

Clinker cost rose 13 per cent, and power and fuel cost went up 15 per cent as pet coke prices climbed 64 per cent. The cement division’s EBITDA per tonne fell to Rs 482 from Rs 712, and its EBITDA margin contracted 490 basis points to 9.8 per cent.

Blended cement made up 86 per cent of sales, while premium products grew 17 per cent to 2.38 million tonnes. The share of the trade channel rose to 82 per cent from 79 per cent.

Green power and coal mine to help contain costs

To contain costs, the company raised green power consumption to 32 per cent from 30 per cent and began extracting coal from its Bikram mine in Madhya Pradesh. The mine is expected to deliver 1.8 lakh tonnes in the second half of the fiscal.

Jute division reports higher revenue and cash profit

In the jute division, revenue rose 17 per cent to Rs 155 crore, and cash profit stood at Rs 13.01 crore against Rs 4.64 crore a year ago, despite a 26 per cent drop in production due to raw jute shortage.

For the first half, net profit fell 27.1 per cent to Rs 153 crore, while revenue rose 8.3 per cent to Rs 5,111 crore.

The company said cement realisation has begun improving from October, but cost pressure is likely to persist and weigh on profitability.

data.title: LPG under recovery may rise to ₹370/cylinder in December 2026
data.description:
The under recovery on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) is expected to rise by roughly 13 per cent on a monthly basis to ₹370 per 14.2 kg domestic cylinder in December 2026.

Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) Director (Finance) Anuj Jain in a post-results analyst call on Saturday said that under recovery on LPG is around ₹309 per domestic cylinder in November 2026 and is likely to hit ₹370 during December.

“The Saudi CP has gone up to $756 per tonne. So as far as my under recovery is concerned, in September 2026 it was ₹184 per cylinder, which went up to ₹229 in October and going forward in the month of November, we see that it would be somewhere in the range of ₹309 per cylinder. In December, it may go to ₹370 per cylinder,” he added.

As of September 30, 2026, IOCL’s cumulative under recovery on LPG was ₹32,505.69 crore.

The other two PSU oil marketing companies, Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) reported under recoveries of ₹17,334.40 crore and ₹18,048.82 crore, respectively.

Under recoveries rise on lower rates

The OMCs are saddled with huge under recoveries on account of selling the cooking fuel--used by more than 33 crore households--at below the prevailing market rates.

IOCL’s September quarter (FY27) net profit more than doubled to around ₹22,503 crore as lower crude oil prices and higher refining margins helped off-set losses from selling petrol, diesel and LPG below market rates.

The country’s largest fuel retailer said that Q2 FY27 profitability was largely driven by temporary decline in crude oil prices from mid-June to mid-August and robust margins from petrochemicals and gas.

“However, profitability in upcoming quarters may be adversely impacted by inventory losses due to potential fall in crude oil prices with normalization of the situation in the Middle East,” it has warned.

data.title: Hoping Rubio revisits India next year: US envoy Sergio Gor says "exciting deliverables" leading upto G20 Summit
data.description:
Atlanta, Oct. 31 -- United States Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, on Saturday said that the US seeks to present "exciting deliverables" ahead of the G20 Summit in December as he highlighted State Secretary Marco Rubio's recent visit to India.

Speaking to ANI in Atlanta, Gor said, "For us, it is important that leaders are engaged at the highest level. As you saw, Secretary Rubio visited India twice in six months, and we are hoping he comes back again next year. There is never a shortage of things to work on. The trip was heavily focused on commercial diplomacy and energy."

"Leading up to the G20, we hope to have some very exciting deliverables, and we are working very closely and rapidly on those behind the scenes," he added.

Marco Rubio earlier concluded his India visit from October 20-21 in the backdrop of negotiations on a proposed bilateral trade agreement and expanded energy cooperation.

In Mumbai, Rubio held talks with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on the India-US strategic partnership. The visit also drew attention to potential investment by Reliance Industries in a new petroleum processing facility in the United States as Rubio visited Jamnagar.

Meanwhile, ahead of the Quad Meeting in Atlanta, he said that they hope an announcement of a leaders' summit is made at some point among all four nations: India, the US, Australia, and Japan. He emphasised the regular engagement between the four nations.

Sergio Gor said, "The Quad is very important to the United States. It is crucial that we communicate on a regular basis with our partners: with India, of course, and with Japan and Australia. This is the third meeting that we are having at this level, the ministerial level. We had our first meeting in Delhi, a second meeting in Manila, and now this third meeting here in Atlanta."

"The hope is that this leads to the finalisation and announcement of a leaders' summit at some point among all four leaders. There is so much that happens within the Quad. We have regular touchpoints almost weekly, so it is very important that there is engagement at the highest levels as well," he added.

EAM Jaishankar took part in the QUAD Foreign Ministers' meeting in Atlanta today alongside Marco Rubio.

data.title: Jaipur Court rejects Inventiva publisher Nitin Naresh's anticipatory bail in Terra Invest case
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- In a significant development in the ongoing legal dispute involving Terra Invest founders Ankiti Bose and Krishan Rattan, a Jaipur sessions court has rejected the anticipatory bail plea of Inventiva publisher Nitin Naresh in a criminal case arising from allegations of extortion, criminal intimidation and conspiracy linked to communications concerning the investment firm.

Additional Sessions Judge Renuka Singh Hudda, Jaipur Metropolitan-II, passed the order on October 28, observing that the material on record and the circumstances of the case did not warrant pre-arrest protection while the investigation remained incomplete. The court also took note of separate Delhi High Court proceedings concerning disputed publications about individuals associated with Terra Invest.

The case stems from a complaint filed by a representative of Terra Vision Investments LLC, who alleged that threatening emails demanded money in exchange for refraining from publishing further adverse material concerning the investment firm and individuals associated with it.

The court considered allegations relating to emails dated August 26 and September 3, 2026, and a payment of Rs.11,700 allegedly deposited into a bank account held in the name of Nine Network Private Limited, the company that owns Inventiva.

The order refers to earlier Delhi High Court proceedings concerning publications about individuals associated with Terra Invest, including its founding partners Bose and Rattan. However, the bail ruling does not establish that the alleged conduct formed part of a wider conspiracy targeting the founders.

According to the complaint detailed in the order, the complainant is the India representative of Terra Vision Investments LLC and operates the investment firm's official email account.

The complainant alleged that emails received on August 26 and September 3, 2026, demanded money and threatened further adverse publications if the demands were not met.

According to the complaint, Rs.11,700 was deposited through a cash deposit machine at an HDFC Bank branch in Jaipur on September 3 into an account held in the name of Nine Network Private Limited. The complainant alleged that the payment was made in the hope that the demands and threats would stop, but another demand followed shortly afterwards.

The court observed that the case diary and material placed before it indicated a connection between the alleged demands, the threat of further publications and the amount deposited into the company's account.

It also noted Naresh's defence that the account was operated online and that the money had been deposited into it without his knowledge. However, the court observed that the record did not contain material showing that he had attempted to return the amount on that basis.

Naresh's counsel denied that he had sent the emails, demanded money or threatened the complainant. The defence also argued that there was no evidence establishing that the email account used to make the alleged demands belonged to him.

Counsel further submitted that Naresh was cooperating with the investigation, that his arrest was unnecessary and that he was willing to comply with any conditions imposed by the court.

The prosecution and the complainant's representatives opposed the plea, arguing that the allegations were serious and that further investigation remained necessary.

The Jaipur court referred to three civil suits before the Delhi High Court in which interim orders had been passed concerning publications about individuals associated with Terra Invest.

The order records that Naresh and other defendants had been restrained from publishing further material covered by the Delhi High Court's directions where such publications could interfere with the plaintiffs' legal rights.

The earlier proceedings included interim orders dated August 24 and September 14, 2026, concerning specified articles and further publications allegedly containing defamatory imputations against individuals associated with the investment firm.

The proceedings form part of the wider legal dispute involving Inventiva and Terra Invest, including individuals associated with the investment firm such as Ankiti Bose and Krishan Rattan.

However, the Delhi High Court's interim orders concern the civil claims before it and do not, by themselves, establish the criminal allegations being investigated in Jaipur. The Jaipur court considered the earlier proceedings while examining the circumstances of the dispute and the allegations forming the basis of the criminal complaint.

The order records that, according to the case diary, Naresh allegedly threatened the complainant's advocate outside court on October 26, 2026.

The court noted that advocate Garvit Khandelwal had lodged a separate complaint against Naresh at Sadar Police Station in Jaipur on the same date in connection with the alleged threat.

The allegation was among the circumstances referred to in the order while the court considered the anticipatory bail application. The separate complaint does not, by itself, establish that the alleged threat occurred.

After considering the material and the rival submissions, the court observed that the dispute between the parties concerned adverse publications and communications, while the present criminal case related to allegations of money being demanded in exchange for refraining from publishing such material.

The court referred to Supreme Court judgments on anticipatory bail, including the need to consider the nature and gravity of the allegations, the presumption of innocence and the requirements of an effective investigation.

It held that the circumstances of the case did not justify granting Naresh pre-arrest protection while further investigation remained pending.

The court accordingly dismissed his application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

The FIR, registered at Shastri Nagar Police Station in Jaipur, invokes Sections 308(2), 308(3), 351(2), 61(2) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

The rejection of anticipatory bail is not a conviction or a final determination of guilt. The allegations against Naresh and the other accused remain subject to investigation and adjudication in accordance with law.

Binance says the 10 assets its users hold most are now backed 1:1. The list covers BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC.

That is normally a routine reassurance. This time it follows a security incident that reportedly cost the exchange around $6.34 billion, so the statement carries more weight than usual.

The confirmation came on October 31, 2026. Binance said the top 10 user assets are fully covered after it resolved the losses from the incident.

The research for this report says the exchange has covered approximately 90% of the total impact. The money came from a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), plus corporate funds.

The remaining 10% is still open. Those losses are mostly tied to lower-liquidity tokens, and Binance is still buying them back through market and OTC channels.

The list itself is worth a look. Four of the 10 assets are dollar-pegged stablecoins: USDT, USDC, USD1, and RLUSD. The rest mix the two largest crypto assets, Binance's own BNB, SOL, XRP, and ZEC.

Binance published a new Proof of Reserves (PoR) snapshot at 00:00 UTC on October 31, 2026. A more detailed verification proof is anticipated by November 3, 2026.

That proof is expected to use zk-SNARKs and Merkle trees. The goal is to let users confirm independently that their balances are backed 1:1 or better.

The previous snapshot gives a useful baseline. On October 1, 2026, reserve ratios for major assets sat at or above 100%.

BTC came in at 100.35%. ETH sat right on the line at 100.00%, and USDT was at 103.88%.

Customer assets on Binance totaled approximately $129.4 billion as of early October. On-chain reserves came to about $135.8 billion, slightly above net liabilities.

The October 31 snapshot should show how those ratios held up after the incident. The November 3 proof is when outside verification becomes possible.

Withdrawals were paused during an internal security review. They are scheduled to restart on November 1, 2026, in phases, one token at a time.

For users, the order of events matters. Binance announced the backing on October 31, withdrawals begin reopening November 1, and the verification proof is expected by November 3.

Customers will be able to move some funds before they can check the cryptographic proof.

The biggest open item is the 10% of losses not yet covered. Binance says the gap sits mostly in lower-liquidity tokens, so major holdings appear protected while holders of smaller assets wait.

The verification proof is the next real test. A full backing claim on October 31 is a statement, while a checkable proof on November 3 is evidence.

There are limits to keep in mind. Proof of reserves shows assets on hand at a moment in time, and its value depends on the liabilities side being complete and accurate.

For now, the claim is clear and the timeline is set. Users should watch three things: the order in which tokens reopen, the November 3 proof, and whether the remaining 10% gets closed out.

Eli Lilly reported Q3 revenue of $24.40B, up 39% Y/Y, beating the $22.42B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $7.48 beat the $5.60 estimate. Growth was driven by strong demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound. The company raised its FY2026 revenue outlook to $91B–$92B.

data.title: CCI Clears Niel's $5.5 Bn Vodafone Stake Acquisition, 3 Other Deals
data.description:
The regulator also approves transactions involving Navi, Aditya Birla Renewables and Adani Energy Solutions

The Competition Commission of India (CCI) on Friday approved four corporate transactions, including French telecom billionaire Xavier Niel's proposed acquisition of a 16.2 per cent stake in UK-based Vodafone Group PLC for 5.1 billion euros.

The Vodafone transaction is being executed through Vega SAS, a French holding company and subsidiary of Maya SAS, Niel's family investment vehicle.

Under an agreement first announced in July, Vega SAS is acquiring the stake from Emirates Telecommunications Group Co PJSC. Upon completion, Vega SAS will become the single largest shareholder in Vodafone Group.

Vodafone India Link

Although Vega SAS does not have direct business operations in India, the transaction required clearance from the Indian competition regulator because of Vodafone's domestic presence through its joint venture, Vodafone Idea.

Under Indian competition laws, global acquisitions that cross specified financial or ownership thresholds require CCI clearance to assess their potential impact on competition in domestic markets.

The investment comes as Vodafone Group undergoes corporate restructuring across its European and African operations. The company has divested its Spanish and Italian businesses and completed a network merger in the UK.

Alongside the Vodafone transaction, the CCI approved three other deals involving companies in the financial technology, renewable energy and power infrastructure sectors.

In the fintech sector, the regulator approved the acquisition of a stake in Navi by MIH Payments Holdings BV.

The acquirer is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of global investment group Prosus NV. It operates as an investment holding vehicle, with its portfolio companies having business operations in India.

Navi Ltd is the holding company of the Navi Group, which offers consumer-facing financial products and services through its subsidiaries via a unified mobile application.

Renewable Energy Deal

The CCI also approved Aditya Birla Renewables' acquisition of Solenergi Power from Shell Overseas Investment BV.

Solenergi is a Mauritius-registered holding company with strategic interests in several solar and wind power generation entities across India.

In another transaction, the CCI approved Adani Energy Solutions' acquisition of 100 per cent of IntelliSmart Infrastructure from the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and Energy Efficiency Services.

Adani Energy Solutions and IntelliSmart operate in advanced electricity metering infrastructure. IntelliSmart also deploys smart gas meters.

data.title: Michael Saylor Compares Bitcoin’s Financialization To Rockefeller’s Oil And Edison’s Electricity, Calls It ‘A Good Thing’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Saylor believes growing competition among Bitcoin-focused companies and financial products is healthy.
  • Strategy reported a record $19.12 billion third-quarter net income, or $44.75 per diluted share.
  • With a U.S. capital markets framework expected in 12 months, Saylor sees tokenization as Bitcoin's next frontier.

Michael Saylor, Executive Chairman at Strategy (MSTR), said that Bitcoin (BTC) is being financialized in the same way that oil and electricity have been, and that the shift will help the asset grow.

Saylor was responding to a question from an analyst in the Q&A on Strategy’s third-quarter earnings call on Thursday. A growing number of firms and products built on Bitcoin was a sign of a healthy industry, not a threat, he said.

As more players come in, the price will go up and the industry will get bigger, he said. The number of people who benefit will grow, as will the number of companies and products, he said.

Saylor Invokes Rockefeller, Edison

Saylor cited two of America’s most renowned industrialists to support his argument. He said worrying about rival Bitcoin products was "kind of like saying, well, in the electricity business, I'm really concerned, Mr. Edison, that other companies also want to create electric motors, or use electricity."

He went on adding, "Or I'm really concerned, Mr. Rockefeller, that other people want to actually build petrochemical products that use oil. Doesn't that bother you?"

"It's like oil got financialized, electricity got financialized, and Bitcoin's getting financialized, and it's not a bad thing," he said. "It's a good thing, right? And it'll turn out to be a great thing."

Record Quarter Backs Bet

Saylor's comments came as Strategy reported a record quarter. The company said in its earnings release that it owned 848,517 Bitcoin as of Oct. 25.

The company reported third-quarter net income of $19.12 billion, operating income of $21 billion or $44.75 diluted per share. Saylor said its stock rose 76% in the quarter compared to a 43% gain in Bitcoin, with Strategy now being the fourth largest equity issuer in the U.S.

The company also said it had put its Stretch preferred stock (STRC) back on the mend. The release said it bought back $2.04 billion of the shares and built up $5.07 billion in U.S. dollar assets.

MSTR’s price closed over 7% on Friday, amid broader weakness due to the Binance (BNB) hack. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MSTR remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, as chatter around it remained at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

Tokenization The Next Frontier

Saylor also linked financialization to tokenization, the process of placing securities on a blockchain to enable freer trading. Speaking on it, Saylor said Strategy has backed offshore tokenization firms such as Apex and Saturn, "cheering them on and enthusiastically watching what's happening there."

In the U.S., he said protocols, platforms, and compliant rules are still evolving. “It is not clear to me that every issue has been settled.” However, he expects for a framework to emerge in the next 12 months. "When it happens, it'll happen pretty quick," he added.

data.title: Lumax Auto’s Anmol Jain sees content per vehicle rising 10-15% by FY29 on premiumisation
data.description:
Lumax Auto Technologies expects the value of components supplied per vehicle to increase by 10-15% by 2028-29 (FY29), as automakers add more features, localise production and adopt green-fuel technologies. Managing Director Anmol Jain said the company currently supplies components worth ₹70,000-75,000 per passenger car and ₹20,000-22,000 per two-wheeler.

The company expects content per vehicle to rise further by 2030-31 (FY31)- 2031-32 (FY32), supported by premiumisation and an expanding product portfolio. Lumax Auto is also investing in its mechatronics business, which includes electrical and electronic components, body control modules, switches and sensors, to benefit from the growing electronic content in vehicles.

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Broadcom, Moderna and Abbott among top picks

Wall Street analysts issued fresh round of upgrades and downgrades. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Broadcom gets bullish rating from D.A. Davidson

D.A. Davidson upgraded Broadcom to Buy from Neutral and upped its price target on the stock to $400 from $350.

“Our reading of the Anthropic S1 leads us to believe the IPO will proceed, Anthropic will raise its capital, and next year OpenAI will raise more capital in its own IPO, allowing Broadcom to meet its expectations for the next couple of years,” DA Davidson analyst Gil Luria wrote.

“At the current 16x multiple on 2027 EPS, AVGO is trading as if the chances of that happening are near zero, which creates significant upside if those deals both materialize,” Luria added.

William Blair is latest to downgrade Moderna on valuation

William Blair became the latest brokerage to downgrade Moderna to Market Perform from Outperform., citing valuation concerns following a late-stage win for its cancer shot developed with Merck .

Noting that Moderna is “up 545% year-to-date and up nearly 250% since the positive INTERPATH-001 trial news announced in August,” William Blair analyst Myles Minter downgraded the stock.

“Although we are incrementally more confident in success given the magnitude of efficacy shown in adjuvant melanoma, development in these additional tumors is not without meaningful clinical and biological risk,” Minter wrote.

Abbott downgraded on guidance cut

Argus Research cut its 12-month rating on Abbott to Hold from Buy, citing the company’s recent decision to trim its full-year growth outlook.

With its Q3 2026 results last week, Abbott set its full-year outlook for comparable sales growth at about 6% down from 6.5% - 7.5% previously, an indication of slower growth in its key growth drivers—electrophysiology and diabetes care, according to analyst David Toung.

“The company faces pricing pressure in markets in which it seeks reimbursement coverage for its products,” Toung wrote, adding it also faces tariff-related costs, and “in the near term, it faces operational risks as it seeks to control costs while addressing supply chain issues.”

data.title: Your stock portfolio increasingly hinges on the bond market - and the midterm elections
data.description:
By Joy Wiltermuth

Tech stocks in late October caught the cold that for months has been a drag on the corporate bond market

Early voting for the U.S. midterm elections in Brooklyn on Oct. 24, 2026.

Your stock portfolio increasingly hinges on what happens in the bond market - and the midterm elections.

Tech stocks in late October caught the cold that for months has been a drag on the corporate bond market.

Poorly performing high-quality "hyperscaler" debt has become a feature - not a bug - of credit markets this year, as buyers of corporate debt struggle to keep up with the capital needs of the AI juggernaut.

"The bond market has a cold. The equity market may have a cold; and the culprit comes from tech," said George Catrambone, head of fixed income, Americas, at DWS, on Friday.

The tech selloff sharpened Friday, landing giants like Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOG), Meta (META,) Intel (INTC), Oracle (ORCL) and SpaceX (SPCX) all in the red, along with semiconductor SOX stocks and other AI hot spots EWY in the market.

Stock market gains have relied on tech in recent years. But bond portfolios also now hinge on tech borrowing, upping the stakes for all things AI to pay off, as planned.

Concerns about the industry's $1 trillion in expected yearly capital expenditures aren't new. Yet investors this week began rewarding those willing to tap the breaks on heavy debt issuance. There's also been swift backlash for others.

Oracle's beleaguered stock finished the week higher after executives indicated a lighter borrowing load for AI going forward. Shares of Alphabet were punished on signs that AI's advance may encroach on a crucial part of its business, even as its data-center spending push continues.

The recent shift in tone also speaks to why investors welcomed Microsoft's (MSFT) new $25 billion bond on Thursday. The company carries higher credit ratings than the U.S. government, has issued less debt than its peers and reported positive free-cash flow of $18.6 billion during earnings this week.

Of note, Microsoft's 10-year tranche of bonds priced at a yield of roughly 5.5%. That compares with the 10-year Treasury yield BX:TMUBMUSD10Y at 4.93% on Friday, according to FactSet. Not every big tech company is expected to get as favorable of pricing.

"Of course it's going to see good demand," said Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at OnePoint BFG Wealth Partners, of Microsoft's bond deal. Yet for most companies borrowing to build AI infrastructure, the cost of capital has gone up, he added.

Higher borrowing costs can eat into future growth, not only for tech stocks, but the U.S. economy. Companies deemed a greater risk of not repaying their debts have been punished in October.

This come as AI-related debt supply has been on a blistering pace of more than $400 billion this year, according to the latest Goldman Sachs estimates, more than double the volume of 2025.

The rush for funding has increased the cost of capital. Cracks in riskier parts of the corporate "junk bond" market and among neoclouds like CoreWeave (CRWV) have grown more apparent. The change has caught the U.S. central bank's attention.

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh spoke to the trend on Wednesday after the central bank opted not to hike interest rates in October.

"Interest rates get in the cracks, interest rates affect directly or indirectly, almost everything," Warsh said Wednesday. "You've seen market participants that are discriminating between the kinds of investments they want to make," he added.

Boockvar told MarketWatch he thinks the Fed might not hike rates in December if the market selloff picks up more steam. Fewer Fed rate increases could help households juggling hot inflation, high gas prices and increased borrowing costs. Mortgage rates could ease.

Friday was month-end, which can trigger limited liquidity and exaggerated moves. The jitters around stocks were evident as Wall Street's Cboe Volatility Index VIX, or "fear gauge," surged in the afternoon, before ending the session nearly 13% higher at 19.42.

Until recently, the AI supply deluge had been siphoning off demand for U.S. government debt since this summer, pushing up benchmark 10-year Treasury yields BX:TMUBMUSD10Y to a 24-year high of 5.3% in early October. But buyers flooded back to the Treasury market when AI tech stocks began to lurch lower.

"Treasurys are finally getting a flight-to-safety [bid] that's long overdue," said Catrambone at DWS.

Market volatility around the U.S. midterm elections could make any new planned equity raises trickier to pull off. Big market selloffs also make placing new debt deals in the hands of investors harder.

The S&P 500 SPX shed 1.8% on Friday, but was still 10.7% higher on the year. Total returns for the ICE BofA U.S. Corporate index turned more negative over the summer as the AI debt deluge intensified along with rates volatility. The corporate bond index was sitting on a negative -0.95% yearly return through Oct. 29, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Negative returns can hurt when companies keep asking investors to provide blank checks for AI, especially when borrowing costs have increased, capital has begun to be more rationed and free-cash flow at many of Silicon Valley's marquee companies has become rather scarce.

"A lot more scrutiny is going on in the bond market," said Matt Wrzesniewsky, head of fixed-income client portfolio Management at Vanguard.

The increased scrutiny isn't only because of credit concerns. Opposition to AI datacenters has been a growing point of worry for many, but not all voters.

Any moratoriums on building datacenters that stem out of the midterms could trigger less capital flowing to the AI build-out, said Catrambone at DWS.

Hints of any slowdown in AI spending could clobber the S&P 500, as MarketWatch's Jamie Chisholm wrote in early October. Questions also would start piling up around the checks already written for the AI build-out.

-Joy Wiltermuth

data.title: Sazmining starts selling Proto mining boards to individual Bitcoin miners
data.description:
Bitcoin mining began as a hobby for people with spare computers and a tolerance for noisy bedrooms. Nearly two decades later, the industry belongs to warehouse-scale operators, and a few companies are trying to coax individuals back in.

The latest attempt comes from Sazmining, a Wyoming-based mining-as-a-service provider. On October 16, 2026, it began selling Proto immersion hashboards directly to individuals. The pitch is a way to earn BTC without running loud, power-hungry machines at home. The fine print is a payback period that, under current assumptions, could stretch past six years.

The hardware is a Proto hashboard developed by Block. Until now, it was mostly available to large mining operators.

Each Proto board delivers approximately 204 TH/s, or 204 trillion hashes per second. It does so at an efficiency of 15 J/TH, meaning it uses 15 joules of energy for every trillion hashes. Multiply the two figures and you get a power draw of about 3,060 watts per board.

The boards use immersion cooling. Instead of fans blowing air across hot chips, the hardware sits in a non-conductive liquid that pulls heat away.

Pricing starts at $4,187 per unit. Buyers who pay in crypto get the price cut to $3,978.

Sazmining also offers financing. Customers can put down $1,397, then make 18 monthly payments of $155 at 0% interest. Run the numbers and the financed total lands exactly at $4,187.

Owning the board is only part of the cost. Sazmining takes a 15% management fee on the Bitcoin each board produces.

Electricity is passed through to the customer at approximately $0.063/kWh.

Under current assumptions, one board could take more than six years to recoup its initial cost. The next Bitcoin halving is expected to extend that timeline further.

A halving cuts the reward miners receive for each new block in half. The next one is expected roughly 76,000 blocks from now.

Ivo Georgiev, founder and CEO of crypto wallet company Ambire, offered a sober read on the opportunity. He mined Bitcoin in 2011 while still in high school.

"It's still hard to make money as an individual miner, and it's not going to get any easier," Georgiev said.

Sazmining's launch arrives as Bitcoin's network hashrate has bounced back above 1,000 EH/s. As of October 30, 2026, network hashrate sat around 1,076 EH/s. Mining difficulty stood at 148.36T.

For perspective, one Proto board at 204 TH/s represents about one five-millionth of the network's current hashrate.

Some large mining operators have been diverting resources toward AI workloads. Their data centers, power contracts and cooling infrastructure turn out to be useful for training and running AI models too.

The core appeal of Sazmining's model is access. Individuals can own industrial-grade hardware without managing heat, noise or wiring at home. The company handles operations and takes its cut from the output.

The 0% financing lowers the upfront barrier considerably. A buyer needs $1,397 to get started rather than the full $4,187. Still, the customer carries 18 months of fixed payments while mining revenue fluctuates with Bitcoin's price and network difficulty.

The six-plus-year payback estimate is a warning label in itself. Mining hardware tends to lose its competitive edge as newer, more efficient machines arrive.

Georgiev's assessment frames the trade-off plainly. Retail mining is accessible again, but the math has not become any kinder to the little guy.

data.title: 3 out of 4 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Alphabet and Verizon .

The communications services sector lost over 14% so far this year, compared to the nearly 13% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, four tickers reported results, all of which three reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, two companies exceeded revenue expectations, while two companies trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Alphabet closed over 12% lower on Thursday following the tech giant’s release of the company's third-quarter financial results, which marked its first quarterly earnings miss since Q4 2022. Q3 earnings trailed Wall Street estimates, despite a more than doubling of Google Cloud revenue as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and services surged.

Verizon Communications reported third-quarter revenue and adjusted earnings above analysts’ estimates, as well as stronger subscriber additions and higher margins that helped the telecom company lift its full-year 2026 guidance for a third consecutive quarter.

T-Mobile increased the number of new customers and saw higher average revenue per account (ARPA) leading to a 7.4% increase in third-quarter revenue and a 34% improvement in earnings, both of which beat Wall Street’s expectations.

For the upcoming week, Charter Communications , Live Nation Entertainment , Fox , and News Corp are some communication services names that are scheduled to report quarterly results.
